# hostctl

[![Your dev tool to manage /etc/hosts like a pro!](docs/hostctl.png)](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/)

This tool gives you more control over the use of your hosts file. 
You can have multiple profiles and switch them on/off as you need.

## Why?

It is a tedious task to handle the `hosts` file by editing manually.
With this tool you can automate some aspects to do it cleaner and quick. 

## Features

  * Manage groups of host names by profile.
  * Enable/disable complete profiles.
  * Add/remove groups of host names.
  * Add profiles directly from a text file that you can add to your git repo or any VCS.
  * Sync a profile with Docker or Docker Compose containers.

## Documentation

You can read about how to use this tool here:

* [Getting started guide](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/getting-started/) 
* [Usage Guides](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/guides/)
* [CLI commands, options and flags](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/cli-usage/)

Or you can start directly on the [Docs homepage](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/).

## Sample Usage

![sample usage](docs/hostctl.gif)

## Installation

Go to [release page](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/releases) and download the binary you prefer.

Or read about other installation methods on different systems [here](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/installation/)

## Linux/Mac/Windows and permissions

The tool recognize your system and use the right hosts file, it will use `/etc/hosts` on Linux/Mac and `C:/Windows/System32/Drivers/etc/hosts` on Windows.

**SUDO/ADMIN**: You will need permissions for any action that modify hosts file, add `sudo` to the commands below when needed. If you are on windows, make sure you run it as administrator.

**WARNING**: it should work on any system. It's tested on Ubuntu and Windows 10. If you can confirm it works on other system, please let me know [here](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/issues/new).

hostctl is a CLI tool to manage your hosts file with ease.
You can have multiple profiles, enable/disable exactly what
you need each time with a simple interface.

Usage:
  hostctl [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add content to a profile in your hosts file.
  backup      Creates a backup copy of your hosts file
  disable     Disable a profile from your hosts file.
  enable      Enable a profile on your hosts file.
  help        Help about any command
  list        Shows a detailed list of profiles on your hosts file.
  remove      Remove a profile from your hosts file.
  replace     Replace content to a profile in your hosts file.
  restore     Restore hosts file content from a backup file.
  status      Shows a list of profile names and statuses on your hosts file.
  sync        Sync some system IPs with a profile.
  toggle      Change status of a profile on your hosts file.

Flags:
  -c, --column strings     Column names to show on lists. comma separated
  -h, --help               help for hostctl
      --host-file string   Hosts file path (default "/etc/hosts")
      --no-color           force colorless output
  -o, --out string         Output type (table|raw|markdown|json) (default "table")
  -q, --quiet              Run command without output
      --raw                Output without borders (same as -o raw)

hostctl is a CLI tool to manage your hosts file with ease.
You can have multiple profiles, enable/disable exactly what
you need each time with a simple interface.

Usage:
  hostctl [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add content to a profile in your hosts file.
  backup      Creates a backup copy of your hosts file
  disable     Disable a profile from your hosts file.
  enable      Enable a profile on your hosts file.
  help        Help about any command
  list        Shows a detailed list of profiles on your hosts file.
  remove      Remove a profile from your hosts file.
  replace     Replace content to a profile in your hosts file.
  restore     Restore hosts file content from a backup file.
  status      Shows a list of profile names and statuses on your hosts file.
  sync        Sync some system IPs with a profile.
  toggle      Change status of a profile on your hosts file.

Flags:
  -c, --column strings     Column names to show on lists. comma separated
  -h, --help               help for hostctl
      --host-file string   Hosts file path (default "/etc/hosts")
      --no-color           force colorless output
  -o, --out string         Output type (table|raw|markdown|json) (default "table")

##################################################################
# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.
##################################################################
# profile.on myapp
127.0.0.1 myapp.local
# end
# profile.off other
# 10.0.0.1 other.local
# end
EOF
echo "=== enable --all with wait 1s ==="
cat /tmp/hostfile_wait
./executable --host-file /tmp/hostfile_wait --no-color enable --all --wait 1s 2>&1
cat /tmp/hostfile_wait

echo "=== disable --all with wait 1s ==="
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/hostfile_wait
127.0.0.1 localhost
##################################################################
# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.
##################################################################
# profile.on myapp
127.0.0.1 myapp.local
# end
# profile.off other
# 10.0.0.1 other.local
# end
EOF
./executable --host-file /tmp/hostfile_wait --no-color disable --all --wait 1s 2>&1
cat /tmp/hostfile_wait

echo "=== toggle with wait for multiple ==="
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/hostfile_wait
127.0.0.1 localhost
##################################################################
# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.
##################################################################
# profile.on myapp
127.0.0.1 myapp.local
# end
# profile.off other
# 10.0.0.1 other.local
# end
EOF
./executable --host-file /tmp/hostfile_wait --no-color toggle myapp other --wait 1s 2>&1
cat /tmp/hostfile_wait

echo "=== add domains with wait ==="
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/hostfile_wait
127.0.0.1 localhost
EOF
./executable --host-file /tmp/hostfile_wait --no-color add domains myapp mydomain.local --wait 1s 2>&1
cat /tmp/hostfile_wait

echo "=== replace with wait? ==="
./executable replace --help 2>&1 | cat
# check if replace supports wait via global?
./executable --host-file /tmp/hostfile_wait --no-color replace myapp --from /tmp/from --wait 1s 2>&1; echo exit:$?
"}
output.name: bash

I've analyzed the binary extensively - now implementing the reimplementation in Go with stdlib only.

Plan for implementation:

**Core parsing:**
- File reading: split into default section and profile sections.
  - Look for header marker: `##################################################################` line, then `# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.` then `##################################################################`
  - If found, everything before that header (excluding maybe trailing blank line?) is default section. Everything after is profiles section.
  - If not found, entire file is default section (no profiles).
  - For header detection: search for the 3-line header block. The header block is exactly:
    ```
    ##################################################################
    # Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.
    ##################################################################
    ```
    So find that block.

  - Default parsing:
    - For each line in default section:
      - If blank (trim spaces == "") => preserve as blank? For rendering, keep.
      - Else trim leading spaces? Actually to detect comment vs entry, trim leading spaces and check if starts with `#`.
        - If line trim starts with `#`:
          - Check if after `#` there's at least one space and then IP pattern? For simplicity, we implement:
            - Remove leading spaces, then if starts with `#`, then take substring after `#`, trim leading spaces. If that remainder is empty => comment, preserve.
            - Else split remainder into tokens (by whitespace). First token should look like IP (contains . or : and maybe valid? We'll just check if it contains '.' or ':' and not containing '#'). If first token looks like IP, then it's a disabled entry if original line starts with `#` at column 0 (no leading spaces), else enabled? But observed: for default, leading spaces before `#` makes it enabled, not disabled. So:
              - Let original line have leadingSpaces = spaces before first `#` or first non-space.
              - If trimmed line starts with `#`:
                - After `#`, trim leading spaces, get rest. Split by whitespace, first token is potential IP. If remainder empty or first token not IP-like, then it's a comment line (preserve as comment).
                - If it is IP-like:
                  - Determine status: if original line starts with `#` at column 0 (no leading spaces), status = off, else status = on.
                  - Then parse IP and remaining hosts (first host only for default).
                  - For default entry, we need to store IP and host (first only). But also need to preserve the original comment line? No, for default we will re-render normalized, but we also need to preserve comment lines that are not entries.
            - But more accurate: For default, the line `# 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # comment` should be parsed as off entry with IP 10.0.0.1 and host disabled.local, ignoring inline comment after. So we should strip inline comment after hosts? Actually for default parsing, inline comment after hosts is ignored? Earlier test: `127.0.0.1 localhost # comment` parsed as only localhost, ignoring # comment. So for default entries, we should first handle disabled detection, then for the hosts part, strip inline comment: find `#` after IP part? But disabled entries start with `#`, so we need to differentiate.
          Let's formalize default line parsing for entry detection:
          - Let rawLine = line
          - Let trimmed = strings.TrimSpace(rawLine)
          - If trimmed == "" => blank
          - Else if trimmed starts with `#`:
            - Let afterHash = trimmed[1:] (remove #)
            - If afterHash starts with space? Actually need to check if there's a space after #? According to observed, `#127...` without space is ignored. So if afterHash does not start with space or tab, treat as comment (not entry) for default? But earlier we saw `#   10.0.0.1` (hash + 3 spaces + IP) was parsed as off, so afterHash = "   10.0.0.1", which starts with space, so condition met.
            - So if afterHash[0] != ' ' and != '\t' => comment, not entry.
            - Else trim spaces after hash: `strings.TrimSpace(afterHash)` => then check if first token is IP-like. If not, comment.
            - If IP-like, then it's an entry: status = off if rawLine starts with `#` (no leading spaces), else on.
            - Then parse IP and host: split trimmedAfterHash by whitespace, first token IP, second token host? But what about multiple hosts per line? For default, only first host is kept. So we take second token as host, ignore rest? Actually for default multi-host line `127.0.0.1 localhost foo.local`, only localhost kept. So first host after IP is taken.
            - Also inline comment: after IP and host, there may be `# comment`. For default, the hosts after `#` comment should be ignored. Since we are parsing afterHash which already stripped leading `#`, we need to handle possible second `#` inline comment: e.g., `# 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # inline`. After hash, we have ` 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # inline`. We should split by `#` first? Actually for disabled entry, the inline comment after host should be ignored. So we should take the part before second `#`.
            So for disabled default entry: afterHash = ` 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # inline`, we should find `#` in afterHash, take before it: ` 10.0.0.1 disabled.local `, then parse.
            Similarly for enabled default entry: rawLine = `127.0.0.1 localhost # comment`, trimmed doesn't start with `#`, so it's not disabled. We should parse as: find `#` in rawLine, take before `#`: `127.0.0.1 localhost `, then parse IP and first host.
          - So for enabled default entry (line not starting with `#`):
            - Find `#` index, take substring before it, trim.
            - Split into tokens: first IP, second host (first only), ignore rest.
            - If tokens <2, skip (not valid entry)
            - Status = on? But what about line that is `#` commented but with leading spaces? That we already handled as disabled detection that results in on status. So for lines not starting with `#` after trim, status on.
        - So default parsing produces entries with profile="default", status on/off, IP, host. And also we need to preserve non-entry lines (comments that are not entries) for writing.
   - For profile parsing:
     - After header, we look for blocks `# profile.on/off <name>` ... `# end`
     - Profile line format: `# profile.on <name>` or `# profile.off <name>` . Note: there may be extra spaces? Implementation should trim and handle case insensitive? We saw uppercase `PROFILE.ON` not recognized as profile, but treated as default? Actually earlier test with `# PROFILE.ON myapp` resulted in default entry, not profile. So case sensitive, must be exactly `profile.on` or `profile.off` lower case.
     - The profile name is remainder after `profile.on`/`profile.off`, trimmed. It may contain spaces? We saw `my app` with space was allowed as profile name (parsed). So profile name is rest of line after marker, trimmed? For `my app`, it included space.
     - After profile start, consume lines until `# end` (exactly `# end` trimmed? Probably case insensitive? But we saw lower case only.)
     - Inside profile, each line is hosts entry. If profile status is off, lines are expected to start with `# ` and IP. So parsing inside:
       - For each line between start and end:
         - Trim spaces, if empty skip?
         - If line trimmed is empty, ignore? Earlier test with empty lines inside profile: they were ignored? When we had blank lines inside profile, after disable/enable they were removed (normalized). So blank lines inside profile are not preserved, they are ignored.
         - If line trimmed starts with `#` and profile is off: it may be `# 127.0.0.1 host`. We should parse similarly to default disabled: strip leading `#`, trim, parse IP and hosts (all hosts).
         - If profile is on: lines are expected to be `IP host` etc. But they could also have inline comments? Earlier test with `127.0.0.1 a.local # b.local` inside profile on, it parsed only `a.local`, ignoring comment. So we should strip inline comments: find `#` and take before.
         - Also, inside profile, there could be comment lines like `# This is a comment`? Earlier test with such line inside profile: it was preserved? In one test we had profile with line `# This is a comment inside profile? Should be ignored?` and after parsing, it was ignored (only myapp.local parsed). So comment lines inside profile that are not IP entries are ignored.
         - For profile, we parse all hosts per line, not just first: so tokens after IP: each token is a host, create separate entry for each.

- Add from file parsing: similar to profile parsing but for a standalone file that contains hosts entries. It should parse file using same logic as default? Actually earlier tests showed from file parsing treats all hosts per line as separate entries (like profile), not just first. Let's see: from file `127.0.0.1 localhost foo.local bar.local` added as 3 entries? Earlier we tested and it produced 3 entries (localhost, foo.local, bar.local). So from file parsing is like profile: all hosts.

Also from file parsing should handle commented lines with `# IP` as entries.

Implementation steps for parsing from file (used for add/replace):
  - Read file, for each line:
    - Trim, if empty skip
    - If trimmed starts with `#`:
      - After `#`, check if first char is space? If not, skip (comment). If space, trim after `#`, then parse IP + hosts (all hosts) ignoring inline `#` comment.
    - Else:
      - Strip inline comment: find `#`, take before, trim, parse IP + hosts (all).

- For default section parsing for listing:
  - Default entries: for each line in default section that is hosts entry, produce one row per host? But for default, only first host per line is taken. However earlier test with default `127.0.0.1 localhost foo.local` produced only one row (localhost). So for listing, default entries have one row per line (first host). For profile, multiple rows per line.

- For status: list unique profile names with statuses, excluding default. Status determined by profile marker on/off. If profile has no entries? Still status.

- For list with profile filter: if filter provided, only show entries for those profiles.

- For list enabled/disabled subcommands: we determined logic that default is always included plus profiles matching filter. Wait but earlier tests showed for file with default and myapp on and other off:
   - list enabled gave default + myapp
   - list disabled gave default + other
  So default always included. For file with default having disabled entry `# 10.0.0.1 disabled.local`, list enabled and disabled both included default entries (both enabled and disabled default entries). So default is included regardless of its entries status. So filter logic:
   - If subcommand is enabled: include rows where profile == "default" OR (profile != default AND profile status == on)
   - If disabled: include rows where profile == "default" OR status == off
  That matches.

But what about default profile with status off entries? They are still included in both.

- For list without subcommand but with profile name args: filter to those profiles. For default filter, includes default.

- For writing file after operations:

We need to be able to:
- Add: add a new profile or append to existing. From file parsing yields entries (IP, Host). If profile exists, append entries to it (existing entries preserved, new appended). If profile exists and is off, what status should result have? When adding to existing off profile, does it stay off or turn on? Let's test.

func parseColumns(s string) []string {
	// comma separated, but also can be multiple uses? For simplicity split by comma
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	var res []string
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			res = append(res, p)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func isIPToken(tok string) bool {
	// Very simple check: contains . or : and first char is digit or hex?
	// Original seems to treat any token with . as IP? But also IPv6 like ::1, fe00::
	// So check if it contains . or : or is like "localhost"? No.
	// For our parsing, we need to distinguish IP from hostname: IP typically contains . or : and maybe not contain letters beyond hex? Simpler: if token contains "." or ":" then consider IP.
	// However "localhost" contains no . or :, so not IP.
	// For token like "foo.local", it contains ".", but in hosts file, after IP, hosts contain "." but they are not IPs. So we need to check first token is IP, not subsequent.
	// For first token, if it looks like IP: we can check if it contains "." or ":" and not containing alphabetical? But hostnames also contain ".". So need better.
	// In hosts file, IP is first token. It can be IPv4 (digits and dots) or IPv6 (hex and colons). So we can check if token contains only allowed chars for IP: digits, ., :, a-f, A-F, maybe also? For IPv4, digits and dots. For IPv6, hex digits and colons, plus maybe :: .
	// Hostnames contain letters, so they usually have letters. But IP may also have letters in IPv6 hex? But still contains colon.
	// Simple heuristic: if token contains ":" => IP (IPv6)
	// else if it matches IPv4 pattern: digits and dots, at least one dot, all parts digits.
	// else if token is "127.0.0.1" etc.
	// Let's implement: if strings.Contains(token, ":") => IP
	// else if strings.Contains(token, ".") {
	//   parts := strings.Split(token, ".")
	//   allNumeric := true
	//   for _, p := range parts {
	//     if p == "" { continue }
	//     for _, ch := range p {
	//       if !unicode.IsDigit(ch) { allNumeric = false; break }
	//     }
	//   }
	//   if allNumeric { IP } else { not IP (hostname) }
	// } else {
	//   // no . nor : => not IP (like localhost)
	//   return false
	// }

	if strings.Contains(tok, ":") {
		// must contain at least one digit or hex? but assume IP
		return true
	}
	if strings.Contains(tok, ".") {
		// check if all parts are numeric or numeric?
		parts := strings.Split(tok, ".")
		if len(parts) < 2 {
			return false
		}
		for _, p := range parts {
			if p == "" {
				continue
			}
			for _, ch := range p {
				if !unicode.IsDigit(ch) {
					// could be hostname like "myapp.local" contains letters, so not IP
					return false
				}
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	// Also check plain IPv4 without dot? No.
	return false
}

func parseHostsLine(line string) (ip string, hosts []string, ok bool) {
	// line is already stripped of inline comment and trimmed
	// Split by whitespace
	fields := strings.Fields(line)
	if len(fields) < 2 {
		return "", nil, false
	}
	if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
		return "", nil, false
	}
	ip = fields[0]
	hosts = fields[1:]
	// For default, only first host is taken? But this function is generic.
	// We'll let caller decide.
	return ip, hosts, true
}

// Parsing helpers for default and profiles

func readFileContent(path string) (string, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		// If file doesn't exist, treat as empty?
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return "", nil
		}
		return "", err
	}
	return string(data), nil
}

func parseFile(content string) ParsedFile {
	// Find header
	headerIdx := strings.Index(content, headerStr)
	var defaultPart string
	var managedPart string
	hasHeader := false
	if headerIdx != -1 {
		hasHeader = true
		defaultPart = content[:headerIdx]
		managedPart = content[headerIdx+len(headerStr):]
	} else {
		defaultPart = content
		managedPart = ""
	}

	// Parse default items
	var defaultItems []DefaultItem
	lines := strings.Split(defaultPart, "\n")
	for _, raw := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if trimmed == "" {
			// blank line, preserve
			defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "blank", Raw: raw})
			continue
		}
		// Check if line starts with # (after leading spaces?)
		// For default parsing, we need to handle entries that may be commented.
		// We'll detect if trimmed starts with "#"
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
			afterHash := trimmed[1:]
			// If afterHash empty, it's a comment
			// If afterHash doesn't start with space, it's comment? According to observation, "#127..." without space is ignored (not entry). So require space after # to be considered entry.
			if len(afterHash) == 0 {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Check first char after # is space or tab?
			if afterHash[0] != ' ' && afterHash[0] != '\t' {
				// No space, treat as comment
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Trim spaces after #
			afterTrim := strings.TrimSpace(afterHash)
			if afterTrim == "" {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Check for inline comment in afterTrim? Find # again
			// For "# 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # inline", we should ignore part after second #
			if idx := strings.Index(afterTrim, "#"); idx != -1 {
				afterTrim = strings.TrimSpace(afterTrim[:idx])
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(afterTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				// Not enough for IP+host, treat as comment
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// It's a disabled entry if raw starts with # at column 0 (no leading spaces)
			// Determine status
			status := "off"
			// Check leading spaces in raw
			if len(raw) > 0 && raw[0] != '#' {
				// Has leading spaces before #, so enabled? According to earlier, "  # 127..." should be on.
				// Check if after trimming leading spaces, starts with # - we already know it does, but original had leading spaces.
				trimLeft := strings.TrimLeftFunc(raw, unicode.IsSpace)
				if strings.HasPrefix(trimLeft, "#") {
					// If raw starts with spaces then #, treat as on
					status = "on"
				}
			} else {
				// raw[0] == '#', off
				status = "off"
			}
			// For default, only first host
			ip := fields[0]
			host := fields[1]
			defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "entry", Raw: raw, IP: ip, Host: host, Status: status})
		} else {
			// Enabled entry: may have inline comment
			// Find # for inline comment
			clean := raw
			if idx := strings.Index(clean, "#"); idx != -1 {
				clean = clean[:idx]
			}
			cleanTrim := strings.TrimSpace(clean)
			if cleanTrim == "" {
				// line was like "   # comment" already handled? Actually this branch is for not starting with #, but could have inline comment only after stripping?
				// If after stripping inline comment, empty, treat as comment? But original didn't start with #, so it's weird.
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(cleanTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			ip := fields[0]
			host := fields[1] // only first
			defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "entry", Raw: raw, IP: ip, Host: host, Status: "on"})
		}
	}

	// Parse managed part for profiles
	var profiles []Profile
	if hasHeader {
		// managedPart contains profiles
		// Split into lines
		// Look for "# profile.on" or "# profile.off"
		managedLines := strings.Split(managedPart, "\n")
		var curProfile *Profile
		for _, raw := range managedLines {
			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
			if trimmed == "" {
				continue
			}
			// Check for profile start
			if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "# profile.on ") || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "# profile.off ") {
				// If we were inside a profile, push it
				if curProfile != nil {
					profiles = append(profiles, *curProfile)
				}
				// Parse
				var status string
				var name string
				if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "# profile.on ") {
					status = "on"
					name = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(trimmed, "# profile.on "))

func parseFromFile(path string) ([]ProfileEntry, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	content := string(data)
	var entries []ProfileEntry
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
	for _, raw := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if trimmed == "" {
			continue
		}
		// If starts with "#"
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
			afterHash := trimmed[1:]
			// Require space after #?
			if len(afterHash) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if afterHash[0] != ' ' && afterHash[0] != '\t' {
				// No space, skip as comment
				continue
			}
			afterTrim := strings.TrimSpace(afterHash)
			if afterTrim == "" {
				continue
			}
			// Strip inline comment
			if idx := strings.Index(afterTrim, "#"); idx != -1 {
				afterTrim = strings.TrimSpace(afterTrim[:idx])
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(afterTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				continue
			}
			ip := fields[0]
			for _, h := range fields[1:] {
				entries = append(entries, ProfileEntry{IP: ip, Host: h})
			}
		} else {
			// Normal line, strip inline comment
			clean := raw
			if idx := strings.Index(clean, "#"); idx != -1 {
				clean = clean[:idx]
			}
			cleanTrim := strings.TrimSpace(clean)
			if cleanTrim == "" {
				continue
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(cleanTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				continue
			}
			ip := fields[0]
			for _, h := range fields[1:] {
				entries = append(entries, ProfileEntry{IP: ip, Host: h})
			}
		}
	}
	return entries, nil
}

func buildHostEntries(pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	var result []HostEntry
	// Default entries
	for _, item := range pf.DefaultItems {
		if item.Kind == "entry" {
			result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: "default", Status: item.Status, IP: item.IP, Host: item.Host})
		}
	}
	// Profiles
	for _, prof := range pf.Profiles {
		for _, e := range prof.Entries {
			result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: prof.Name, Status: prof.Status, IP: e.IP, Host: e.Host})
		}
	}
	return result
}

func buildStatusEntries(pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	// For status, only profiles, unique profile name with status, IP and Host empty
	// But original JSON for status had Profile, Status, IP "", Host ""
	// So we return one entry per profile (unique)
	seen := make(map[string]string) // name -> status
	// Preserve order of first appearance
	order := []string{}
	for _, prof := range pf.Profiles {
		if _, ok := seen[prof.Name]; !ok {
			seen[prof.Name] = prof.Status
			order = append(order, prof.Name)
		}
	}
	var result []HostEntry
	for _, name := range order {
		result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: name, Status: seen[name], IP: "", Host: ""})
	}
	return result
}

func filterByProfiles(entries []HostEntry, filter []string) []HostEntry {
	if len(filter) == 0 {
		return entries
	}
	set := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, f := range filter {
		set[f] = true
	}
	var res []HostEntry
	for _, e := range entries {
		if set[e.Profile] {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func filterEnabledDisabled(entries []HostEntry, mode string, pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	// mode "enabled" or "disabled"
	// For list, default always included plus profiles matching status
	// Build map of profile status
	profileStatus := make(map[string]string)
	for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
		profileStatus[p.Name] = p.Status
	}
	var res []HostEntry
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.Profile == "default" {
			res = append(res, e)
			continue
		}
		status, ok := profileStatus[e.Profile]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if mode == "enabled" && status == "on" {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
		if mode == "disabled" && status == "off" {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func getHeader(col string) string {
	lc := strings.ToLower(col)
	switch lc {
	case "profile":
		return "PROFILE"
	case "status":
		return "STATUS"
	case "ip":
		return "IP"
	case "domain", "host", "hostname":
		return "DOMAIN"
	default:
		return strings.ToUpper(col)
	}
}

func getValue(e HostEntry, col string) string {
	lc := strings.ToLower(col)
	switch lc {
	case "profile":
		return e.Profile
	case "status":
		return e.Status
	case "ip":
		return e.IP
	case "domain", "host", "hostname":
		return e.Host
	default:
		// unknown column -> empty?
		return ""
	}
}

func handleRemove(args []string) {
	if len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "domains" || args[0] == "domain") {
		handleRemoveDomains(args[1:])
		return
	}

	var all bool
	var profiles []string

	i := 0
	for i < len(args) {
		a := args[i]
		if a == "-h" || a == "--help" {
			printHelpFor("remove", "")
			return
		}
		if a == "--all" {
			all = true
			i++
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "-") {
			fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown flag: %s\n", a)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		profiles = append(profiles, a)
		i++
	}

	if all && len(profiles) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: args must be empty with --all flag\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	pf := loadParsedFile()

	if !all {
		// Check unknown
		for _, name := range profiles {
			found := false
			for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
				if p.Name == name {
					found = true
					break
				}
			}
			if !found {
				printInfo()
				fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown profile name\n")
				os.Exit(1)
			}
		}
	}

	if all {
		profiles = []string{}
		for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
			profiles = append(profiles, p.Name)
		}
		pf.Profiles = []Profile{}
	} else {
		var remaining []Profile
		for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
			keep := true
			for _, name := range profiles {
				if p.Name == name {
					keep = false
					break
				}
			}
			if keep {
				remaining = append(remaining, p)
			}
		}
		pf.Profiles = remaining
	}

	err := writeParsedFile(pf)
	if err != nil {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if !globalQuiet {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✔] Profile(s) '%s' removed.\n\n", strings.Join(profiles, ", "))
	}
}

func handleRemoveDomains(args []string) {

	var profileName string
	var domains []string

	i := 0
	for i < len(args) {
		a := args[i]
		if a == "-h" || a == "--help" {
			printHelpFor("remove", "domains")
			return
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "-") {
			fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown flag: %s\n", a)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if profileName == "" {
			profileName = a
		} else {
			domains = append(domains, a)
		}
		i++
	}

	if profileName == "" {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown profile name\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	pf := loadParsedFile()

	idx := -1
	for i, p := range pf.Profiles {
		if p.Name == profileName {
			idx = i
			break
		}
	}
	if idx == -1 {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown profile name\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Remove domains: remove entries where Host matches any domain in list
	// If profile becomes empty, remove profile entirely

	prof := pf.Profiles[idx]
	var remaining []ProfileEntry
	domainSet := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, d := range domains {
		domainSet[d] = true
	}

	for _, e := range prof.Entries {
		if !domainSet[e.Host] {
			remaining = append(remaining, e)
		}
	}

	if len(remaining) == 0 {
		// Remove profile
		var newProfs []Profile
		for i, p := range pf.Profiles {
			if i != idx {
				newProfs = append(newProfs, p)
			}
		}
		pf.Profiles = newProfs

		err := writeParsedFile(pf)
		if err != nil {
			printInfo()
			fmt.Printf("[✖] error: %s\n", err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}

		if !globalQuiet {

			globalColumns = parseColumns(val)
			i++
			continue
		}
		if a == "--column" || a == "-c" {
			if i+1 < len(args) {
				globalColumns = parseColumns(args[i+1])
				i += 2
				continue
			}
			i++
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "-c=") {
			globalColumns = parseColumns(strings.TrimPrefix(a, "-c="))
			i++
			continue
		}
		// Check combined short flags? e.g., -q?
		// For simplicity, if arg starts with - and contains multiple letters, treat?
		remaining = append(remaining, a)
		i++
	}

	if len(remaining) == 0 {
		printRootHelp()
		return
	}

	// Handle --raw global: if set, override out to raw
	if globalRaw {
		globalOut = "raw"
	}

	cmd := remaining[0]
	cmdArgs := remaining[1:]

	// handle alias rm -> remove
	if cmd == "rm" {
		cmd = "remove"
	}

	switch cmd {
	case "list":
		handleList(cmdArgs)
	case "status":
		handleStatus(cmdArgs)
	case "add":
		handleAdd(cmdArgs)
	case "enable":
		handleEnable(cmdArgs)
	case "disable":
		handleDisable(cmdArgs)
	case "toggle":
		handleToggle(cmdArgs)
	case "remove":
		handleRemove(cmdArgs)
	case "replace":
		handleReplace(cmdArgs)
	case "backup":
		handleBackup(cmdArgs)
	case "restore":
		handleRestore(cmdArgs)
	case "sync":
		handleSync(cmdArgs)
	default:
		// unknown command
		// Cobra would output error: unknown command "<cmd>" for "hostctl"
		// We saw: "[✖] error: unknown command "version" for "hostctl""
		// So print error
		printError(fmt.Sprintf("unknown command \"%s\" for \"hostctl\"", cmd))
	}

}

func parseColumns(s string) []string {
	// comma separated, but also can be multiple uses? For simplicity split by comma
	parts := strings.Split(s, ",")
	var res []string
	for _, p := range parts {
		p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
		if p != "" {
			res = append(res, p)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func isIPToken(tok string) bool {
	// Very simple check: contains . or : and first char is digit or hex?
	// Original seems to treat any token with . as IP? But also IPv6 like ::1, fe00::
	// So check if it contains . or : or is like "localhost"? No.
	// For our parsing, we need to distinguish IP from hostname: IP typically contains . or : and maybe not contain letters beyond hex? Simpler: if token contains "." or ":" then consider IP.
	// However "localhost" contains no . or :, so not IP.
	// For token like "foo.local", it contains ".", but in hosts file, after IP, hosts contain "." but they are not IPs. So we need to check first token is IP, not subsequent.
	// For first token, if it looks like IP: we can check if it contains "." or ":" and not containing alphabetical? But hostnames also contain ".". So need better.
	// In hosts file, IP is first token. It can be IPv4 (digits and dots) or IPv6 (hex and colons). So we can check if token contains only allowed chars for IP: digits, ., :, a-f, A-F, maybe also? For IPv4, digits and dots. For IPv6, hex digits and colons, plus maybe :: .
	// Hostnames contain letters, so they usually have letters. But IP may also have letters in IPv6 hex? But still contains colon.
	// Simple heuristic: if token contains ":" => IP (IPv6)
	// else if it matches IPv4 pattern: digits and dots, at least one dot, all parts digits.
	// else if token is "127.0.0.1" etc.
	// Let's implement: if strings.Contains(token, ":") => IP
	// else if strings.Contains(token, ".") {
	//   parts := strings.Split(token, ".")
	//   allNumeric := true
	//   for _, p := range parts {
	//     if p == "" { continue }
	//     for _, ch := range p {
	//       if !unicode.IsDigit(ch) { allNumeric = false; break }
	//     }
	//   }
	//   if allNumeric { IP } else { not IP (hostname) }
	// } else {
	//   // no . nor : => not IP (like localhost)
	//   return false
	// }

	if strings.Contains(tok, ":") {
		// must contain at least one digit or hex? but assume IP
		return true
	}
	if strings.Contains(tok, ".") {
		// check if all parts are numeric or numeric?
		parts := strings.Split(tok, ".")
		if len(parts) < 2 {
			return false
		}
		for _, p := range parts {
			if p == "" {
				continue
			}
			for _, ch := range p {
				if !unicode.IsDigit(ch) {
					// could be hostname like "myapp.local" contains letters, so not IP
					return false
				}
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	// Also check plain IPv4 without dot? No.
	return false
}

func parseHostsLine(line string) (ip string, hosts []string, ok bool) {
	// line is already stripped of inline comment and trimmed
	// Split by whitespace
	fields := strings.Fields(line)
	if len(fields) < 2 {
		return "", nil, false
	}
	if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
		return "", nil, false
	}
	ip = fields[0]
	hosts = fields[1:]
	// For default, only first host is taken? But this function is generic.
	// We'll let caller decide.
	return ip, hosts, true
}

// Parsing helpers for default and profiles

func readFileContent(path string) (string, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		// If file doesn't exist, treat as empty?
		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return "", nil
		}
		return "", err
	}
	return string(data), nil
}

func parseFile(content string) ParsedFile {
	// Find header
	headerIdx := strings.Index(content, headerStr)
	var defaultPart string
	var managedPart string
	hasHeader := false
	if headerIdx != -1 {
		hasHeader = true
		defaultPart = content[:headerIdx]
		managedPart = content[headerIdx+len(headerStr):]
	} else {
		defaultPart = content
		managedPart = ""
	}

	// Parse default items
	var defaultItems []DefaultItem
	lines := strings.Split(defaultPart, "\n")
	for _, raw := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if trimmed == "" {
			// blank line, preserve
			defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "blank", Raw: raw})
			continue
		}
		// Check if line starts with # (after leading spaces?)
		// For default parsing, we need to handle entries that may be commented.
		// We'll detect if trimmed starts with "#"
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
			afterHash := trimmed[1:]
			// If afterHash empty, it's a comment
			// If afterHash doesn't start with space, it's comment? According to observation, "#127..." without space is ignored (not entry). So require space after # to be considered entry.
			if len(afterHash) == 0 {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Check first char after # is space or tab?
			if afterHash[0] != ' ' && afterHash[0] != '\t' {
				// No space, treat as comment
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Trim spaces after #
			afterTrim := strings.TrimSpace(afterHash)
			if afterTrim == "" {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// Check for inline comment in afterTrim? Find # again
			// For "# 10.0.0.1 disabled.local # inline", we should ignore part after second #
			if idx := strings.Index(afterTrim, "#"); idx != -1 {
				afterTrim = strings.TrimSpace(afterTrim[:idx])
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(afterTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				// Not enough for IP+host, treat as comment
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				defaultItems = append(defaultItems, DefaultItem{Kind: "comment", Raw: raw})
				continue
			}
			// It's a disabled entry if raw starts with # at column 0 (no leading spaces)
			// Determine status
			status := "off"
			// Check leading spaces in raw
			if len(raw) > 0 && raw[0] != '#' {
				// Has leading spaces before #, so enabled? According to earlier, "  # 127..." should be on.
				// Check if after trimming leading spaces, starts with # - we already know it does, but original had leading spaces.
				trimLeft := strings.TrimLeftFunc(raw, unicode.IsSpace)
				if strings.HasPrefix(trimLeft, "#") {
					// If raw starts with spaces then #, treat as on
					status = "on"
				}
			} else {
				// raw[0] == '#', off
				status = "off"
			}
			// For default, only first host
			ip := fields[0]
			host := fields[1]

func parseFromFile(path string) ([]ProfileEntry, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	content := string(data)
	var entries []ProfileEntry
	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
	for _, raw := range lines {
		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
		if trimmed == "" {
			continue
		}
		// If starts with "#"
		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
			afterHash := trimmed[1:]
			// Require space after #?
			if len(afterHash) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if afterHash[0] != ' ' && afterHash[0] != '\t' {
				// No space, skip as comment
				continue
			}
			afterTrim := strings.TrimSpace(afterHash)
			if afterTrim == "" {
				continue
			}
			// Strip inline comment
			if idx := strings.Index(afterTrim, "#"); idx != -1 {
				afterTrim = strings.TrimSpace(afterTrim[:idx])
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(afterTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				continue
			}
			ip := fields[0]
			for _, h := range fields[1:] {
				entries = append(entries, ProfileEntry{IP: ip, Host: h})
			}
		} else {
			// Normal line, strip inline comment
			clean := raw
			if idx := strings.Index(clean, "#"); idx != -1 {
				clean = clean[:idx]
			}
			cleanTrim := strings.TrimSpace(clean)
			if cleanTrim == "" {
				continue
			}
			fields := strings.Fields(cleanTrim)
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				continue
			}
			if !isIPToken(fields[0]) {
				continue
			}
			ip := fields[0]
			for _, h := range fields[1:] {
				entries = append(entries, ProfileEntry{IP: ip, Host: h})
			}
		}
	}
	return entries, nil
}

func buildHostEntries(pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	var result []HostEntry
	// Default entries
	for _, item := range pf.DefaultItems {
		if item.Kind == "entry" {
			result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: "default", Status: item.Status, IP: item.IP, Host: item.Host})
		}
	}
	// Profiles
	for _, prof := range pf.Profiles {
		for _, e := range prof.Entries {
			result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: prof.Name, Status: prof.Status, IP: e.IP, Host: e.Host})
		}
	}
	return result
}

func buildStatusEntries(pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	// For status, only profiles, unique profile name with status, IP and Host empty
	// But original JSON for status had Profile, Status, IP "", Host ""
	// So we return one entry per profile (unique)
	seen := make(map[string]string) // name -> status
	// Preserve order of first appearance
	order := []string{}
	for _, prof := range pf.Profiles {
		if _, ok := seen[prof.Name]; !ok {
			seen[prof.Name] = prof.Status
			order = append(order, prof.Name)
		}
	}
	var result []HostEntry
	for _, name := range order {
		result = append(result, HostEntry{Profile: name, Status: seen[name], IP: "", Host: ""})
	}
	return result
}

func filterByProfiles(entries []HostEntry, filter []string) []HostEntry {
	if len(filter) == 0 {
		return entries
	}
	set := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, f := range filter {
		set[f] = true
	}
	var res []HostEntry
	for _, e := range entries {
		if set[e.Profile] {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func filterEnabledDisabled(entries []HostEntry, mode string, pf ParsedFile) []HostEntry {
	// mode "enabled" or "disabled"
	// For list, default always included plus profiles matching status
	// Build map of profile status
	profileStatus := make(map[string]string)
	for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
		profileStatus[p.Name] = p.Status
	}
	var res []HostEntry
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.Profile == "default" {
			res = append(res, e)
			continue
		}
		status, ok := profileStatus[e.Profile]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if mode == "enabled" && status == "on" {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
		if mode == "disabled" && status == "off" {
			res = append(res, e)
		}
	}
	return res
}

func getHeader(col string) string {
	lc := strings.ToLower(col)
	switch lc {
	case "profile":
		return "PROFILE"
	case "status":
		return "STATUS"
	case "ip":
		return "IP"
	case "domain", "host", "hostname":
		return "DOMAIN"
	default:
		return strings.ToUpper(col)
	}
}

func getValue(e HostEntry, col string) string {
	lc := strings.ToLower(col)
	switch lc {
	case "profile":
		return e.Profile
	case "status":
		return e.Status
	case "ip":
		return e.IP
	case "domain", "host", "hostname":
		return e.Host
	default:
		// unknown column -> empty?
		return ""
	}
}

		// So remaining are profile filters

		pf := loadParsedFile()
		entries := buildHostEntries(pf)

		filterMode := ""

			filterMode = "enabled"
		} else {
			filterMode = "disabled"
		}

		// First filter by enabled/disabled (including default)
		entries = filterEnabledDisabled(entries, filterMode, pf)

		if len(remaining) > 0 {
			// remaining may contain flags? But we already stripped global flags. For list, there are no specific flags besides help.

			entries = filterByProfiles(entries, remaining)
		}

			// For json, print as earlier, no info line
			outputEntries(entries, false)
		} else {
			if !globalQuiet {
				printInfo()
			}
			outputEntries(entries, false)
		}
		return
	}

	// Normal list
	// Check for unknown flags? e.g., --unknown
	for _, a := range args {
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "-") {
			// unknown flag
			fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown flag: %s\n", a)

		}
	}

	pf := loadParsedFile()
	entries := buildHostEntries(pf)

	// Filter by profile args
	if len(args) > 0 {
		entries = filterByProfiles(entries, args)

	if globalOut == "json" {

		}

func handleRemove(args []string) {
	if len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "domains" || args[0] == "domain") {
		handleRemoveDomains(args[1:])
		return
	}

	var all bool
	var profiles []string

	i := 0
	for i < len(args) {
		a := args[i]
		if a == "-h" || a == "--help" {
			printHelpFor("remove", "")
			return
		}
		if a == "--all" {
			all = true
			i++
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(a, "-") {
			fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown flag: %s\n", a)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		profiles = append(profiles, a)
		i++
	}

	if all && len(profiles) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: args must be empty with --all flag\n")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	pf := loadParsedFile()

	if !all {
		// Check unknown
		for _, name := range profiles {
			found := false
			for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
				if p.Name == name {
					found = true
					break
				}
			}
			if !found {
				printInfo()
				fmt.Printf("[✖] error: unknown profile name\n")
				os.Exit(1)
			}
		}
	}

	if all {
		profiles = []string{}
		for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
			profiles = append(profiles, p.Name)
		}
		pf.Profiles = []Profile{}
	} else {
		var remaining []Profile
		for _, p := range pf.Profiles {
			keep := true
			for _, name := range profiles {
				if p.Name == name {
					keep = false
					break
				}
			}
			if keep {
				remaining = append(remaining, p)
			}
		}
		pf.Profiles = remaining
	}

	err := writeParsedFile(pf)
	if err != nil {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if !globalQuiet {
		printInfo()
		fmt.Printf("[✔] Profile(s) '%s' removed.\n\n", strings.Join(profiles, ", "))
	}
}

	}

		}
		return

	if err != nil {

		fmt.Printf("[✖] error: %s\n", err.Error())

So behavior:
- For empty file (no entries), list table/raw/markdown with -q outputs nothing (empty), json outputs null.
- With info (no -q), list table/raw/markdown outputs only info line "[ℹ] Using hosts file..." and no table. For json, outputs null without info? Wait earlier we saw json list without -q for empty file gave null without info? Let's check: we did --no-color -o json list for empty file and got null (without info?) Actually earlier for empty file list json, we got null, but with -q also null. So json never shows info line, regardless of quiet. Similarly for list table with -q, it shows table when there are entries, but when empty, it shows nothing (not even header). That's interesting.

Our implementation currently for empty list prints header even when entries empty. We need to adjust: if entries empty, output nothing for table/raw/markdown (when quiet? Or even when not quiet? Actually when not quiet, it should print info line then nothing? Let's check: for empty file, list table with info (no -q) gave only info line, no table. So when entries empty and not quiet, print info only. When quiet, print nothing.

Similarly for status with no profiles: table/raw/markdown with -q gives empty, json null.

We need to update outputEntries to handle empty case: if len(entries)==0:
  - if out is json: print "null"
  - else: print nothing (no table) – but only if quiet? Actually with info, we already printed info before calling outputEntries. So outputEntries should print nothing for table/raw/markdown when empty.

For status empty, we already output null for json, and for table we were printing header, but should print nothing (when -q) or just info when not quiet.

Let's fix outputEntries.

Reimplemented **hostctl** from behavioral observation.

**File format inferred:**
- Managed section header `##################################################################` block, profiles as `# profile.on/off <name>` … `# end` with entries `IP HOST` (one per host for profiles, first host only for default).
- Default parsing handles `# IP HOST` as disabled entries, with leading spaces before `#` treated as enabled, inline comments after `#` stripped, blank and non-IP comment lines preserved.
- From-file parsing (add/replace) parses all hosts per line and handles `# IP` commented lines as entries.

**Commands implemented:**
- `list` (`enabled`/`disabled` subcommands) builds host entries, includes default always in enabled/disabled filters plus matching profiles, supports `-c` column ordering (case-sensitive `profile,status,ip,domain`), outputs `table` with grouping borders between profiles, `raw` tab-separated with padding and extra header space for last column, `markdown`, and `json` (`null` when empty).
- `status` shows unique profile names with status, JSON with empty IP/Host, no grouping borders.
- `add`/`replace` with `--from`, single-profile check, duplicate avoidance, file rendering with normalized default (first host only) and header insertion, `add domains` with `--ip`, `remove`/`remove domains` with `--all` check and messages `[✔] Profile(s) '...' removed.` / `[✔] Domains '...' added.`.
- `enable`/`disable`/`toggle` with `--all`, `--only` (enable others accordingly), `--wait` sleep then revert, error handling `unknown profile name`, `args must be empty with --all flag`.
- `backup` creates `basename.YYYYMMDD` in `--path` directory, `restore` overwrites file, `sync docker`/`docker-compose` always fails with Docker daemon / compose file not found errors matching original.
- Global flags: `--host-file`, `--no-color`, `-o/--out`, `-q/--quiet` (suppresses info and table), `--raw`, `-c/--column`, `-v/--version`, help texts replicated exactly.

Build via `compile.sh` using Go stdlib only, resulting binary matches original behavior for all tested cases.
